title: Office 365 MCP Values
description: Values for the Office 365 MCP Helm chart. Python FastMCP server for Microsoft 365. Exposure uses base chart Gateway API routes (no custom Ingress).

mcpConfig.description: Configuration for the Office 365 MCP Server, mapped to environment variables (PUBLIC_BASE_URL, ENTRA_TENANT_ID, ENTRA_CLIENT_ID, TOOLS_PRESET/TOOLS_ENABLED).

publicBaseUrl.description: The externally-reachable OAuth issuer URL that clients are redirected to. Must be https. Example: https://office-365.mcp.unique.app

entra.description: The Entra app registration that users sign in through

tenantId.description: One tenant's ID, or 'organizations' for a multi-tenant (AzureADMultipleOrgs) registration. With 'organizations', any user from any Entra tenant can sign in. The server validates each access token against its own tenant's issuer, and calls Graph in that tenant. The server rejects 'common' and 'consumers' at startup, because personal Microsoft accounts have no Microsoft 365 mailbox or Teams.

clientId.description: The client ID of the Entra app registration that users sign in through.

clientSecret.description: The app registration's client secret, from the office-365-mcp-entra-application Terraform module's client_secrets[key].key_vault_secret_name output. This secret is also the key material for the OAuth state rows, so rotating it costs every signed-in user one re-login. The chart automatically collects fromSecretProvider into its SecretProviderClass, so it needs no separate secretProvider.vaults entry.

tools.description: The tool surface that this deployment runs. Set exactly one of preset or enabled. The enabled tools decide which delegated Microsoft Graph permissions Entra asks every user to consent to at sign-in. So, this field has no default deliberately. Choosing 'every tool' must be a deliberate choice, not what a deployment gets by not choosing one.

preset.description: Which tools this deployment runs, as a named surface. 'teams' is every Teams tool. Each other name is one use case, and README's preset table says what each costs a tenant in permissions and admin consents. Set this or enabled, never both. Narrowing a live deployment is free. Widening it makes every signed-in user sign in again.

enabled.description: Which tools this deployment runs, as a comma-separated list of tool names, for a surface no preset covers. A deployment does not name get_me in this list, because it is always on. So, no deployment asks for less than User.Read. Set this or preset, never both. Name at least one tool. An empty value is a selection that says nothing, so the server refuses to start. This early check is the difference between a failed helm install and a crash-looping pod. GET /manifest and the startup log print the resolved tools, the exact delegated permissions, and which of them need admin consent. That list is what an Entra administrator must grant.

folder.description: Grafana folder name for the dashboard
